citations.review_text:
Broforce is one of those games that somehow manages to be hilarious without anybody really saying anything.  The humor is all in the animations, ridiculous action, explosions, and parody characters, and a lot of the Bros are genuinely really well done. I used to play this with my brother back in 2015, and finally coming back years later and finishing it on my AYN was a great time.

The game can get frustrating as hell, but usually in a fun way. The final boss especially was brutal, and there were definitely moments where an attack felt basically impossible to escape, but honestly that chaos is part of what makes Broforce work. I constantly had the “one more level” feeling, especially because I wanted to see which character I’d unlock next.

My main complaint is that I wish there were more things besides new Bros to unlock or mess around with. There are already a ton of characters, but more weapons, modifiers, modes, upgrades, or other gameplay variety would’ve made it even better.

Still, an amazingly good game that had me sucked in till the very end. Funny as hell, addictive, chaotic, and way more polished than something this stupid has any right to be.

the last satah fight is such a slog and doesnt feel fair. its just luck and also not really fun like the rest of the game. the game itself is so cool and all the characters feel unique and new. theres so many and im loving it. still seeing new ones. great time

citations.review_text:
Played this game back in 2016. I had pretty good memories of it and decided to play it again in 2026. What a nightmare.

It's not strictly a bad game, but you need to have the right expectations to fully enjoy it. The game is marketed differently, which is my main gripe. I think it was marketed as a co-op shenanigan, but in reality it's a hardcore platformer.

The first one or two hours are fun. You blast through the maps with your favorite movie characters. It feels fresh and rewarding.

Then everything goes to hell (literally). Environmental hazards and traps are everywhere, and everything explodes. The game always seems to spawn the hero who's least suited for the task, so you just keep dying until the right character finally appears. Only to die from some random explosion anyway.

On top of that, Stage 15 drags on for far too long, with no option to quit mid-game. I was already burned out by that point.

The cherry on top? Serious desync issues, which are incredibly frustrating considering you already have to deal with all the other ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ happening on the screen.

[quote]Reviewed by [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45820397-DetotatedGamer/]Detotated Gamer[/url][/quote]

A pretty good game until the aliens showed up (they were just annoying), cool to see characters being references from other games/movies. The possibility to destroy the environment is fun and the characters unique weapons and special abilities (or lack of) make the game more interesting and sometimes challenging. One big negative is that at points because of all the chaos going on on the screen it becomes difficult to follow the character. Overall the game is kind of frustrating, but still fun especially with friends. Love the 2D pixel art. Solid 7 bros/10.

It's 2026 and everyone is asking: "What's your opinion of Broforce?"
Well I'll tell you. I hate it.
I hate it because it's so close to being a classic, like painfully inches from perfection.
But there are so many bad design decisions that just make the game incredibly unfun.
The tone and art and feel of the game are all incredibly good, but no one wants to hear about that. 
THE BAD
1) I can't keep track of where I am. The visual chaos of the game, while endearing, makes it so I have to keep my eyes locked on the player character or I just lose them completely. That means I can't watch for anything coming my way.
2) There is too much stuff that kills you. Dying to enemy bullets is wonderful. Dying to a stupid falling block that got shoved loose because you barely grazed it, is not. Falling in a giant pit because the jump mechanics are so unwieldy and vary between Bros isn't fun either.
3) The destructable enviroments weren't a good idea. Yeah I said it. And I mean it. Being able to pick axe through a level and skip everything isn't good, it isn't fun, and requires no creativity.
4) The options in this game are terrible. It's hard to even get to the button layout menu, you have to be fully exited from the game and in the main menu, otherwise you can't see that there is a DASH BUTTON THAT THE GAME NEVER TELLS YOU ABOUT. But don't worry dashing only works some of the time.
5) Stuff randomly explodes. Sounds great right? except the part where you have no idea what is going to happen in a level without serious foreknowledge. I'm okay with having to learn a level but how the rules and physics of the game randomly seem to change, is maddening. The AoE of exploding barrels seems to be random, sometimes 1 square radius, or sometimes up to 4. Good luck figuring out how to meatboy your way through the levels with that kind of craziness.
6) Like anyone cares, this game is way past the point where it's going to get updated. If it had a few more modern design decisions it would be…

Over a decade from its release, Broforce remains an interesting artifact of gaming circa 2015, while also remaining a mostly decent though fairly frustrating ridiculous action movie trope mega-menagerie.

In terms of gameplay, Broforce is a mash-up between side-scrolling shooters, with a lo-fi Super Meat Boy aesthetic blended with hyper-destructable levels that are almost always in the middle of actively being destroyed. The near constant flow of explosions both purposefully made and occurring due to semi-random systems creates a kind of constant chaos that has a fun factor to it, but can often be difficult to predict or deal with for the player, which in turn can become a massive frustration factor. The fairly far-removed "camera angle" that sees the Bros as tiny single "square" units on these large maps helps alleviate this a bit, but the explosions and enemies and bullets can quickly overflow any amount of reaction time ability even the twitchiest gamer can deal with. 

However, this is where the game's main hook kicks in, with the large cast of Bros, as each death (as well as each "rescue/extra life") changes your player character to one of the many heroes modeled after Action-Movie All-Stars, from the Rocketeer to the Terminator to Rambo to Snake Plisken to many, many more. Each has different functionality in how they attack, in both their basic attack, their limited "grenade" attack, and even their melee attacks or jumping depending on the character (Indiana Brones, for example can use his whip to grapple around levels). Because of the (EXTREMELY) high number of Bros drawn from more references than you'd expect, this leads to very high player-character function variability, but because the bro chosen on death or rescue is RANDOM, the player also has to learn to master every character to deal with the game's challenges or end up frustrated when they get one they don't like or prefer. Again, a key element of what makes the game fun is also a source of frustr…

citations.review_text:
This game holds a special place in my heart. I played it with friends back in high school, and I had so much fun. Such fond memories from simpler times. Now grown but not quite matured, I was quite excited to see the Broforce Forever update a while back, so I thought I'd give it another go, just for old time's sake.

It's a run-and-gun with bravado at the forefront, that teeters between the lines of campiness and charm. Parodies of 90s era action heroes sent on a mission to liberate lands and exterminate terrorist threats. While satirical, it pays great homage to the parodies that inspire it, and happened to make a really great game while doing so. All the bros play differently, and the constant switching between deaths and rescues means you'll always have to adapt to each of their playstyles throughout the levels.

The only things that come between you and the helicopter at the end of the level is the environment and the hordes of enemies; and while they are dangerous in tandem, I'd argue the former is the bigger threat. YOU are the deadlist thing on screen, and the mayhem you'll cause will domino into an unpredictable mess of explosions and sharp objects. The environment is very much destructible, which can work to your advantage as much as it can detriment. You will get yourself killed if not too careful, and likely cause the deaths of your friends as well. Levels can get very chaotic, very fast.

This game might be an oldie, but it's a goldie. It's well worth its price, and does go for cheap on sales. Get you and your friends in a session and kick some terrorist butt in retro fashion. Broforce Forever. o7

The Bottom Line
Broforce is an absolute masterpiece of over-the-top, 80s and 90s action-movie parody that delivers hours of high-octane fun. Having put over 40 hours into the PS4 version before picking it up on Steam, I can confidently say this is an absolute must-buy for couch co-op. Between the iconic, action-hero-themed "Bros," fighting terrorists, and literally going to hell to fight the devil, the game turns classic action tropes into pure comedy gold (complete with health items like "Vitaminz"—which are clearly just steroids with tape slapped over the label). It serves up endless chaotic camaraderie and accidental collateral damage with the boys. If you're playing purely solo, it’s still an enjoyable run-and-gun side-scroller, but the true magic of this game only unlocks when you have friends sitting next to you on the couch.

The Crunch
The gameplay is fast, chaotic, and heavily relies on fully destructible terrain and dynamic physics. The character pool is massive, and half the fun is discovering the unique, hilarious mechanics built into each Bro. Whether it’s starting out classic with Rambro, using Indiana Brones’ whip to latch onto ledges and zip around, or firing the Noisy Cricket with Bro In Black to launch yourself completely across the stage from the gun's recoil, every Bro feels distinct. The random Bro-swapping mechanic keeps you on your toes, forcing you to adapt your playstyle on the fly while trying not to accidentally blow up the floor directly beneath your teammate's feet.

The Flow
The campaign moves at a breakneck pace, throwing short, action-packed missions at you before capping them off with absurd boss fights and high-stakes extractions via helicopter. Having played through tens of hours of this game, the humor and chaos never get old. While a solo run can feel a bit repetitive after a while, the unpredictability of local co-op keeps the pacing fresh, hilarious, and high-energy from start to finish.

The Setup
Played on the Steam…

Almost every part of a level in Broforce is destructible, and many elements generate explosions and chain reactions. The game works as a single-player game, but encourages and advertises 4-player co-op. 

The intent is emergent, unpredictable gameplay - thinly controlled chaos and spectacle with a veneer of tactical decision-making. Nothing in Broforce is really "hard" or even gets harder as it goes along. Everything in Broforce is ridiculous and inherently risky. You influence what happens and enjoy the shenanigans. 

There are 39 playable characters. The more you play, the more you unlock, and the game randomly gives you one of the "Bros" at the start of a stage and then randomly changes that Bro every time you get a 1-up (which is rendered as rescuing a captured Bro). You might start a stage as "Indiana Brones" and then change to the Brominator before switching to Bronan the Barbarian and wrapping things up with McBrover. 

The vibe in Broforce is "adapt to what's happening," which is why it feels so much like a rogue-like, even though it isn't one. 

Entertaining. Maybe a little too chaotic for its own good... but that's sort of the whole identity of the game. 🤣

citations.review_text:
1) Bought the game
2) Killed Satan
3) Became friends with Jesus
4) Downloaded game and had a blast

Jokes aside, its really fun platformer game where 99% of map can be destroyed either by player or explosives/enemies.
There is a lot of different characters linked to pop culture etc. many enemy types and variants, enourmous amount of bosses and acceptable amount of 'consumables' that help progress through the game. Everything I just mentioned is done flawlessly-the design, the idea, the final product. It just coulnt be better.
Campaing also has bonus levels that unlock even more content like more consumables or special abilities.
Game has several difficulties to choose from, the hardest are lethat and barely possible to finish ("Die=save deleted"), game has also steam workshop with maps made by players, some are quite nice and feel like base game levels, others are terrible jokes that shouldnt be on this platform at all.
Bugs are pretty rare, and if any happen at all its nothing serious like game crash/freeze or data loss, more like animation glitches at most.
Game is no longer updated which is sad, but devs released one final major update before abandoning the game, which resulted in even more content and fun.
If you dont like playing solo, game has coop option to up to 4x players.

A 2D run-and-gun shooter filled with explosions, destructible environments, and action-movie parody characters. Every “Bro” has a different weapon and ability, which keeps gameplay chaotic, unpredictable, and funny.
The levels are fast and messy (in a good way). It’s simple, over-the-top fun that doesn’t take itself seriously.
it’s absolute chaos in the best way and even better when playing with friends.

Listen up, recruits! I hit the ground running in Broforce and it hit me like a ton of friggin’ C4. Buildings? Boom. Walls? Gone. Enemies? Pulverized. This isn’t a game… it’s a battlefield, and I am the storm. I’m Rambro, I’m B.A. Broracus, I’m every gun, rocket, and fist you’ve ever dreamed of, and when I move, the world shakes.

Every jump is a launch. Every punch is a demolition. Every rocket is justice raining from the heavens. I don’t tiptoe, I don’t hesitate — I run, I fire, I explode, and if anyone gets in my way… they learn the hard way what a bro can do. The ground shakes. The sky explodes. Cows fly like missiles. It’s glorious chaos, and I love it.

Levels don’t stand a chance. Enemies don’t stand a chance. The only rule here is total destruction, maximum firepower, and leaving nothing behind but smoke, fire, and screams of pure victory. Co-op? Even better — more bros, more explosions, more glorious chaos. We don’t strategize… we obliterate.

You want subtlety? Forget it. You want finesse? Forget it. You want to feel like an unstoppable action hero ripping through the world with rockets, fists, and sheer bravado? Then grab your gun, grab your bro, and let’s make this world remember the meaning of the word BROFORCE.

Final rating: BADASS

The hours on this aren't accounting for offline time or something because I've put hundreds of hours over the years and I still come back to this day. I would buy a sequel in an instant, really anything related to be frank. I love all the different environmental interactions, and how the game feels completely different playing alone and with friends.

Game has several difficulties to choose from, the hardest are lethat and barely possible to finish ("Die=save deleted"), game has also steam workshop with maps made by players, some are quite nice and feel like base game levels, others are terrible jokes that shouldnt be on this platform at all.
Bugs are pretty rare, and if any happen at all its nothing serious like game crash/freeze or data loss, more like animation glitches at most.
Game is no longer updated which is sad, but devs released one final major update before abandoning the game, which resulted in even more content and fun.
If you dont like playing solo, game has coop option to up to 4x players.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as featuring extensive environmental destruction, which can occasionally destroy enough of a level to make reaching the final checkpoint impossible.

citations.review_text:
Had this game for a while now. Played it alone, played it in 2, played it on the couch with a full squad, It's always a blast. It's just so wacky but at the same time unique. The map destruction and various characters make it really fun to just ♥♥♥♥ around and try wacky strats, especially in less linear levels.

Only thing i would say as a negative is that sometimes levels/bosses get a bit frustrating especially toward the end of the game. Not a problem while beating it alone, but it can kill a more casual vibe with your friends.

A really solid fun game to play either alone or with friends. For its price it's pretty good. On sale it's a steal.

When unspecified TERRORISTS working for THE DEVIL HIMSELF threaten vaguelly-defined FREE WORLD and even bring up LEGALLY-DISTINC COPIES OF XENOMORPHS to the planet, it is up to BROFROCE, the team of GREATEST AMERICAN HEROES to stop them with huge amounts of violence and destruction.

BROFORCE is retro run and shoot game, where you control a team of Bros that seem oddly similiar but legally distinc from various heroes from action movies and shows, and an occassional horror character. Each Bro has its own style of fighting and even Bros who use similair methods play different - Brade, Brode, Broheart and Brolander, for example, all use swords, but their prefered strategies and special moves differ enough to change the experience completely. You die from one hit, but during each level you can rescue captured Bros, who take place of your character and you get new random bro if you die with extra lives gained this way. This keeps the game from being stale, as you need to adjust your strategy every time you die and get a new character. Unless you're playign Tank Bro, since if she summons her tank, anybro can ride it. Worth noting is also that there is a lot of enviromental damage you can do in this game and it is very much possible you destroy so much of the level you cannot reach the final checkpoint. The story mode is enjoyable by constantly introducing new enemies, be them terrorists, aliens or undead, so it never gets boring, and the custom level community keeps the replayability up.

No other game have I sunk so many hours into because it is great to keep my eyes and hands occupied when I need to focus on lsitening to something. For that alone this romp of fun deserves a recommendation.

If you love fast-paced action, epic explosions, and a heavy dose of nostalgia from 80s and 90s action movies, Broforce is the perfect game for you! Developed by Free Lives Games, this shoot 'em up puts you in control of a squad of over-the-top patriotic heroes, each inspired by iconic movie characters.

With addictive gameplay, charming pixel art graphics, and chaotic cooperative multiplayer, Broforce delivers pure adrenaline and fun. Get ready to demolish environments, face absurdly challenging enemies, and save the world in style.

Whether playing solo or with friends, Broforce is an explosive blast of entertainment from start to finish! 🔥💥
